questions.q: What is the real, specific record type that holds the top-level entry a user sees when they expand your custom application in the navigator?
questions.explain: The Application Menu, a sys_app_application record, is the top-level entry; it's created automatically with the scoped app.

questions.q: Which field on a Module record nests it under the correct top-level Application Menu, rather than leaving it floating loose?
questions.explain: A module's Application menu field points back at its parent sys_app_application record, which is what nests it correctly.

questions.q: A module needs to open one specific, always-the-same configuration record rather than a list of many records. Which Link type fits?
questions.explain: Record opens one specific record directly, which is the right fit for a single configuration or settings record rather than a list.

questions.q: What does the Order field on a Module actually control?
options: Whether the module requires a role to be visible
Which application scope the module belongs to
Where the module falls relative to its sibling modules inside the same Application Menu
Whether the module links to a table or a UI Page
questions.explain: Order is a plain number; a lower value places the module higher relative to its siblings under the same Application Menu.

questions.q: How does a Role set on a Module differ from the scope-level protection covered in Chapter 5?
options: They are the same mechanism described with two different names
A module's Role controls which logged-in users even see that entry in the navigator; scope controls whether code outside the app can call into it at all
A Role on a module only affects modules with Link type set to URL
Scope only applies to tables, while Role only applies to Script Includes
questions.explain: A module's Role is navigator-level visibility for users; application scope is a separate, code-level access boundary from Chapter 5.
